subject: Hosted API: data residency, retention and deletion details
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@helixfi.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - residency / TTL / deletion questions

Hi Olga,

Quick set of questions from our compliance team as we evaluate Redwood for production:

1) Can we ensure Helix data stays in the EU region only (no replication outside EU)?
2) What are the default retention windows for request payloads, logs, and embeddings stored by the hosted API?
3) If we issue an erasure request for a tenant, how long until data is fully removed from backups/snapshots?
4) Are there options for a shorter TTL than the default (policy-level or per-tenant)?

Appreciate a short written response we can include in our security pack.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Compliance, Helix Financial
sophie.lang@helixfi.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@helixfi.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 May 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - residency / TTL / deletion questions

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can include in your pack; I also attached a short DPA summary and a tenant erasure form for audit purposes.

1) Regional residency: Our hosted API supports region-scoped tenancy. For Helix we can pin your tenant to the EU region (Frankfurt or Dublin) so that primary data storage and active copies remain within the EU. We do not geo-replicate tenant data to other regions unless explicitly configured for multi-region failover; any cross-region replication is controlled by your account admin and documented in the tenancy settings.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Request payloads & generation inputs: default 30 days.
- Inference logs (routing/latency/trace metadata): default 30 days.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: by default 90 days unless you opt in to persistent storage policies.
- Audit logs (security/audit trail): retained 365 days for enterprise customers by default; can be extended under contract.

3) Erasure timeline:
- Immediate: We mark the tenant data for deletion within 24 hours of a verified erasure request.
- Primary stores: logical deletes are completed within 72 hours.
- Backups & snapshots: retained per backup schedule; most backups are recycled on a 90-day cadence. We guarantee that customers' erased data will be purged from live backups within 90 days; if you require an accelerated schedule we can discuss a special purging process (subject to support and contractual terms).

4) Shorter TTLs / tenant controls:
- Per-tenant TTL: Yes — we can configure shorter tenant-level TTLs for request payloads/embeddings (for example, 7 or 14 days) at account provisioning or via a support ticket for existing tenants.
- API-driven erasure: We provide a deletion API and a manual deletion request workflow (see attached form).

Notes on caching & ephemeral state: our runtime uses in-memory KV caches for token/KV acceleration; these caches are not persisted to long-term storage and are cleared on instance termination.

Compliance & proof points: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant; we maintain WORM-protected audit records and can provide attestations as part of our security pack.

If you want a short single-page statement we can sign and return for your vendor list.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2025 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - residency / TTL / deletion questions

Olga — quick internal note before we send the signed statement: Sophie asked specifically about snapshots created during incident response and whether those are covered by the 90-day backup purge. For Helix (finance vertical) we should offer a shorter backup purge SLA if possible. Can you confirm whether engineering can support a 45-day guaranteed purge for customers on an enterprise contract?

Also suggest we include the API endpoint and example curl for deletion in the follow-up to Sophie.

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Strategic Accounts
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@helixfi.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2025 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - residency / TTL / deletion questions

Hi Sophie — looping back with two clarifications after an internal check:

• Backups & incident snapshots: Standard commitment is purge within 90 days, but for enterprise customers we can include a 45-day backup purge SLA in the contract addendum; this requires an explicit clause and an operational playbook (we'll draft).

• Deletion API example (tenant-level):
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/delete\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"requestor":"Helix Compliance", "request_id":"req-20250502-1"}'

After the request is validated we return an erasure token and a ticket number; primary deletes complete within 72 hours and backup purge per SLA (default 90 days, 45 days available by contract).

I've attached the DPA summary and a deletion request form you can use to initiate a verified erasure. If you'd like, Ben and I can join a 30-minute call with your compliance team to walk through the wording and sign the statement.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: data_deletion_request_form.docx]
